Cell-cycle-driven epigenetic resetting maintains meristematic cell fate for shoot branching
abstract: Cell proliferation generally promotes differentiation, whereas proliferative quiescence maintains stem cell identity—a paradigm well-established in adult mammalian stem cells. Here we report that in Arabidopsis bud precursor cells, meristematic cell fate maintenance depends on active cell-cycle progression. We identify two opposing mechanisms that balance trimethylated histone H3 Lys27 levels to regulate transcription of the shoot meristem marker gene SHOOT MERISTEMLESS ( STM ). On one hand, two classes of transcription factors recruit Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) to epigenetically silence STM . On the other hand, cell proliferation reduces trimethylated histone H3 K27 levels to counteract this silencing. We demonstrate that inhibiting cell division suppresses STM expression and promotes differentiation. The interplay between these forces establishes a cell-cycle-coupled epigenetic resetting mechanism that sustains pluripotency. This cell fate switch is bistable; both modelling and experimental data confirm that prolonged quiescence triggers irreversible differentiation. We propose that in plants, sequence-dependent PRC2 recruitment enables precise silencing of fate-determining genes, while cell proliferation maintains pluripotency through periodic resetting of epigenetic marks.

title: Phloem conductivity decrease over 300 million years of fern evolutionary history
abstract: The radius of sieve elements, the conducting cells in the phloem — the sugar transport tissue in plants — varies greatly in extant ferns and has changed over the course of their evolution. We show that sieve element radius has decreased in fern evolution, a change that probably directly affected the capacity of phloem to transport sap.

title: Remaking wheat with a thousand cuts
abstract: CRISPR is deployed against centromeric retrotransposons in hexaploid bread wheat to trigger rapid and extensive changes to the chromosomes, effectively rewriting the karyotype.

title: Use of two-colour autoluminescent reporters enables quantitative imaging of gene expression in plants
abstract: In glowing plants, monitoring the ratio of two luminescence colours, rather than luminescence intensity, enabled quantitative plant physiology measurements despite interference of metabolism in light emission. This two-colour approach bypasses metabolic ‘noise’ to provide a consistent, accurate reading of plant immune and hormonal responses, as validated with both fungal and bacterial bioluminescence systems.

Enhanced forest temperature regulation covaries with greater heat resistance of ecosystem photosynthesis
abstract: Forests regulate the land surface temperature (LST) through biophysical processes and subsequently mitigate climate warming. However, how this ecosystem-scale surface thermal regulation capacity (TRC) has evolved globally remains unknown. Here we use 20 years (2001–2020) of satellite-based LST observations to provide global evidence that TRC has significantly strengthened in global forests, as indicated by widespread declines in both the LST–air temperature slope (−0.0014 ± 0.0003 °C °C −1 yr −1 ; P < 0.01) and the LST–air temperature difference (−0.0268 ± 0.005 °C yr −1 ; P < 0.01). The observed enhancement of TRC is primarily associated with increased tree cover and warming trends. Species-rich forests exhibit higher TRC, probably through an enhanced transpiration/evapotranspiration ratio. Moreover, spatial and temporal variations in TRC, which characterize ecosystem-scale surface energy partitioning, covary with the optimal temperature for forest photosynthesis and with photosynthetic resistance to thermal stress. Our findings underscore the critical importance of conserving and restoring diverse forests to regulate surface energy balance and safeguard terrestrial carbon uptake in a hotter world.

title: Widespread reversal of vegetation resilience in permafrost ecosystems
abstract: Rapid warming in permafrost regions is destabilizing ecosystem functioning, raising concerns about how vegetation withstands and recovers from natural disturbances. Yet the evolution of vegetation resilience (VR) under permafrost degradation remains poorly understood. Analysis of satellite observations from 2000 to 2023 reveals that, despite continued greening, VR increased initially but underwent a widespread reversal after 2008. This reversal was most strongly associated with intensifying atmospheric drought, while analyses of ocean evaporation and atmospheric moisture transport suggest that changes in oceanic moisture supply may have contributed to post-2008 drying. Wildfires further amplified VR losses in disturbed areas. Current models fail to capture this observed reversal, suggesting an underestimation of climate risks to high-latitude carbon sinks. Even with continued greening, the post-2008 decline in VR signals a destabilization of plant carbon uptake, highlighting a decoupling between greening and resilience in permafrost regions. Our findings identify atmospheric drought as a key constraint on permafrost vegetation stability and suggest that ocean–land moisture interactions are involved in modulating this process. Improved representation of atmospheric drought, moisture transport and disturbance effects in predictive models is therefore essential for assessing the future stability of permafrost ecosystems.
